title: Determined Combinations: Rate Constants From Equilibrated Snapshots
innovation_hook: Fast reversible pairs equilibrate before the first snapshot, so kf and kr are individually invisible in the data and any (kf,kr) with the right sum fits; only the equilibrium ratio kf/kr (fixed by the conserved total mass and the observed split) is a determined combination. The strong solution reports that determined ratio at a safely-fast scale instead of curve-fitting both rates to flat data.
strategies: trivial: report the same flat generic rate constant for every edge, ignoring all snapshot data

greedy: two-point log-slope finite-difference rate estimate on the source species of every edge, treating each edge as an isolated decay -- correct for slow chain edges, but collapses fast reversible pairs to near-zero rates since their snapshots are already flat at equilibrium

strong: least-squares log-linear regression (all snapshots) for slow chain edges; for fast reversible pairs, read off the determined kf/kr ratio from the equilibrium concentration split and assign a safely-large, T1-calibrated absolute scale instead of fitting it
invalid: emit non-finite rates for every edge
